experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, tacos de canasta, and traditional Mexican street food. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients used in authentic Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
experiences.description: Visit one of the world's greatest anthropology museums, home to the famous Aztec Sun Stone and vast collections spanning Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations including Maya, Aztec, Olmec, and Toltec cultures. A must-see for anyone interested in Mexican heritage.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood Walk & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Stroll through the bohemian cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse the local artisan market, and enjoy a traditional tlayuda or tamale from street vendors in the central plaza.

experiences.name: Tacos & Mezcal Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Spend an evening hopping between the trendy taquerias and mezcalerías of Roma Norte. Try tacos al pastor, suadero, and barbacoa paired with artisanal mezcal. This neighborhood blends traditional Mexican flavors with a vibrant modern food scene.

experiences.name: Teotihuacán Pyramids Day Trip
experiences.description: Take a short bus ride from Mexico City to the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacán. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and explore the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. One of the most awe-inspiring archaeological sites in the Americas.
experiences.location: Teotihuacán, State of Mexico (60 km northeast of Mexico City)

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique stay in Centro Histórico after landing and settling in.
day_by_day.afternoon: After check-in, take a leisurely walk to the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Metropolitan Cathedral — both free to view from outside. Stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the historic atmosphere of Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.evening: Wander along Calle Regina, a lively pedestrian street in Centro Histórico filled with street performers, local vendors, and budget-friendly eateries. Grab a seat at an outdoor café, enjoy the energy of the neighborhood, and ease into your first night in Mexico City.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before landing or grab a quick snack upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Stop at a street taco stand near the Zócalo — look for tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for around 15–25 MXN per taco. Try Tacos El Huequito on Calle Bolívar, a legendary local spot.
meals.dinner: Head to Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén nearby for an affordable and authentic dinner. Try a comida corrida (set meal with soup, main, and drink) at one of the market stalls for around 80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 13:00. Budget roughly 1–1.5 hours for immigration, baggage, and transit to Centro Histórico via Metro Line 1 (very affordable at ~5 MXN). Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Carry small bills for street food vendors.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its adjacent museum (entry ~80 MXN). This ancient Aztec temple complex sits right in the heart of Centro Histórico and is one of the most significant archaeological sites in Mexico. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the ruins and the museum's impressive collection of artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes (free to view the exterior and ground-floor lobby — upper floors have a small fee). Then head to the nearby Alameda Central park to relax among locals. From there, explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) and the surrounding streets of the historic center. Visit the free Museo del Estanquillo (folk art and popular culture) on Calle 5 de Mayo.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant nightlife around Plaza Garibaldi, about a 15-minute walk from your hotel, where Mariachi bands perform live. Enjoy the atmosphere for free — simply stand in the plaza and listen. Then wind down with a stroll back through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico.

meals.breakfast: Visit a local market or fondita near your hotel for a classic Mexican breakfast: chilaquiles or huevos rancheros with coffee for around 60–90 MXN. Try Café de Tacuba on Calle Tacuba, a historic and affordable local institution.
meals.lunch: Grab a torta (Mexican sandwich) or quesadillas from street vendors near Alameda Central for 30–50 MXN. The area has many budget-friendly lunch spots.
meals.dinner: Dine at one of the budget cantinas or taquerías around Plaza Garibaldi. Try pozole or birria for a hearty and authentic meal for around 80–130 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Sundays offer free entry to many national museums — if you adjust your schedule, keep this in mind. Wear comfortable walking shoes as most sights are within walking distance. Stay aware of your belongings in crowded tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 2) to Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most charming and bohemian neighborhoods. Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online (entry ~270 MXN). Spend 1.5 hours exploring the life and art of Frida Kahlo in her iconic blue house.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Mercado de Coyoacán for lunch and browsing. Explore the Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, Coyoacán's beautiful central squares lined with cafés and artisan stalls. Browse the weekend craft market for unique, affordable souvenirs. Visit the free Museo de Culturas Populares on Avenida Hidalgo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Take an evening walk along Madero Street, one of the most beautiful pedestrian avenues in the city, beautifully lit at night. Stop at the rooftop terrace of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México (free to visit the lobby and see the stunning Tiffany stained-glass ceiling).

meals.breakfast: Eat at your hotel or a nearby café — pick up fresh pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a local panadería for under 40 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas from the market stalls for 60–100 MXN. This is one of the best budget food experiences in the city.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro Histórico, try a traditional fonda (family-run restaurant) for a comida corrida-style dinner. Look for handwritten menus outside — a full meal with drink costs 80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. Metro is the most budget-friendly transit option (~5 MXN per ride). Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Tlatelolco and visit the Plaza de las Tres Culturas — a fascinating open-air site where Aztec ruins, a colonial Spanish church, and modern architecture coexist. Entry is free. Learn about the significance of this historically important plaza. Then walk to the nearby Mercado de Tlatelolco for a local market experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Tepito neighborhood market (Tianguis de Tepito) for a gritty, authentic Mexico City experience — browse secondhand goods, street food, and local wares. Exercise standard city caution. Alternatively, visit the Mercado de la Ciudadela (Mercado de Artesanías) near Centro for affordable handicrafts, textiles, and souvenirs — great for budget shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and visit the free Museo de la Ciudad de México on Calle Pino Suárez (check hours in advance). End the evening with a walk through the beautifully lit Zócalo at night — the square looks spectacular after dark.

meals.breakfast: Try a classic Mexican breakfast at a local market stall near Centro — tamales with atole (warm corn drink) for around 30–50 MXN, a beloved local morning tradition.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Mercado de Tlatelolco or a nearby fondita — try chiles rellenos or mole enchiladas for 70–100 MXN.
meals.dinner: Visit a local taquería in Centro Histórico for tacos de barbacoa or suadero — one of the most satisfying and affordable dinners in the city at 15–25 MXN per taco. Try Taquería Los Cocuyos on Calle Bolívar, a beloved late-night local spot.

day_by_day.notes: Tepito can be lively — go during daylight hours and keep valuables secure. Mercado de la Ciudadela is a safer and more tourist-friendly alternative for souvenir shopping. The Zócalo at night is a must-see and completely free.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world and an absolute must-see (entry ~80 MXN, free on Sundays). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the incredible collections covering Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations, including the famous Aztec Sun Stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museum, stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's massive and beloved urban park — entry is free. Enjoy the lakes, vendors, and local families enjoying their day. Walk back toward the park's eastern entrance and explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood for window shopping and people-watching before returning to Centro.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in Centro Histórico revisiting your favorite spots. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from street vendors around the Zócalo. Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of the neighborhood's best budget restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Have a hearty final Mexican breakfast at Café de Tacuba or a local fondita near your hotel — order molletes (open-faced bean and cheese toast) or a full Mexican breakfast plate for 70–100 MXN.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and delicious lunch from street vendors near Chapultepec park — elotes (grilled corn), tortas, or tacos for 30–60 MXN. The park area has many affordable options.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last night at a mid-range local restaurant in Centro Histórico. Try mole negro or chiles en nogada (seasonal) at a traditional Mexican restaurant for 150–200 MXN — still very budget-friendly by international standards.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on Day 6 or later, this day works perfectly as a final full day. If departing on Day 5, adjust the afternoon to allow transit time to the airport. The Museo de Antropología is one of the highlights of any Mexico City trip — don't miss it. Keep Metro fare cards loaded for easy travel throughout the day.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approx. 45–60 min by taxi or metro). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the Metropolitan Cathedral. Stroll through the surrounding streets to soak in the colonial architecture and street life.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero, beautifully lit in the evening. Stop at the rooftop bar of Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a drink with stunning views of the Zócalo before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a coffee and pastry at the hotel or a nearby café upon settling in.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and authentic meal at Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén — try tacos de guisado or tlayudas from local market stalls (budget-friendly, ~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Cardenal (Palacio de Correos location) — a beloved mid-range Mexico City institution known for traditional Mexican breakfast and dinner dishes like mole, chiles en nogada, and house-made bread (~$15–25 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the afternoon arrival. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Exchange currency or withdraw pesos at the airport for convenience. The Zócalo area is very walkable from Centro Histórico hotels.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo del Templo Mayor, located steps from the Zócalo. Explore the archaeological ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán and the adjacent museum housing extraordinary pre-Hispanic artifacts. (~2–3 hours, entry ~$5 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio Nacional to admire Diego Rivera's sweeping murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mercado de la Merced or Mercado Jamaica to experience the vibrant sights, sounds, and smells of a working local market.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) area and the lively streets of Centro at night. Attend a free cultural event or live music performance at one of the plazas if available (check local listings). End the evening with a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local fonda near the hotel — chilaquiles, huevos rancheros, or tamales with atole (~$4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Bar La Opera on Avenida 5 de Mayo — a historic cantina with classic Mexican dishes and great atmosphere (~$12–18 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Tacos and antojitos at a well-regarded street taco stand near the Zócalo such as Tacos de Canasta El Güero, or sit-down at Hostería de Santo Domingo, Mexico City's oldest restaurant (~$10–18 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with the Palacio de Bellas Artes visit planned for Day 3. Carry small bills for market vendors and street food.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Palacio de Bellas Artes — admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior and explore the interior murals by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros. The attached Museo del Palacio de Bellas Artes hosts rotating cultural exhibitions (~$3–5 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Avenida Juárez to Alameda Central park for a relaxing stroll. Then take the metro or a short taxi ride to the trendy Colonia Roma or Condesa neighborhoods to explore independent boutiques, bookshops, art galleries, and beautiful Art Deco architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roma/Condesa for the evening — two of CDMX's most vibrant neighborhoods for nightlife and dining. Browse the café and bar scene along Álvaro Obregón or Ámsterdam Avenue.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café de Tacuba in Centro Histórico — a classic, atmospheric café serving traditional Mexican breakfast since 1912 (~$8–12 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Colonia Roma at Contramar (arrive early or book ahead) — famous for tuna tostadas and grilled fish in a buzzy setting (~$18–25 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a casual but acclaimed spot in Condesa such as El Hidalguense for barbacoa, or Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre for creative corn-based Mexican dishes (~$12–20 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Roma and Condesa are best explored on foot. The neighborhoods are about 4–5 km from Centro Histórico — take the metro (Line 1 to Insurgentes) or an Uber for ~$3–5 USD. March weather is typically mild and dry, perfect for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Teotihuacán — the ancient 'City of the Gods' with the iconic Pyramids of the Sun and Moon. Depart early by bus from Terminal Norte (about 1 hour, ~$3 USD each way). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun for panoramic views and explore the Avenue of the Dead (~$5 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the on-site Museo de Sitio. Browse artisan vendors near the site for handmade obsidian crafts and souvenirs before heading back to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico by late afternoon. Relax and freshen up at the hotel. Spend the evening exploring the illuminated historic center — visit the Plaza de Santo Domingo and enjoy the atmospheric streets of the old city at night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab tamales and café de olla from a street vendor before departing for Teotihuacán.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Gruta restaurant at Teotihuacán — a unique mid-range restaurant built inside a natural cave near the pyramids, serving traditional Mexican cuisine (~$15–22 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico in Centro Histórico — a beautiful courtyard restaurant specializing in regional Mexican cuisine from across the country (~$15–25 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Start the Teotihuacán trip as early as possible (ideally by 8:00–9:00 AM) to avoid midday heat and crowds. Wear sunscreen, a hat, and bring water — there is little shade on the pyramids. Buses depart regularly from Terminal Norte (take metro Line 5 to Terminal Norte station).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest museums, housing the Aztec Sun Stone, Maya artifacts, and collections spanning all of Mexico's pre-Hispanic cultures. Allow 2–3 hours minimum (~$5 USD entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas. Visit the hilltop Castillo de Chapultepec (National History Museum) for sweeping views of the city and fascinating exhibits on Mexican history (~$4 USD entry). Wind down with a walk through the park's gardens and lake area.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to Centro Histórico or explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby for a memorable farewell dinner. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at artisan shops or the Ciudadela market before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a café in Centro, such as Café El Popular — open 24 hours, beloved by locals for pan dulce, café de olla, and egg dishes (~$5–8 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch near Chapultepec at a casual spot in Polanco — try Los Panchos for carnitas, a legendary Mexico City institution (~$10–15 USD per person).
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at Pujol (book well in advance) for a world-class modern Mexican tasting menu (~$80–120 USD per person), OR a more budget-conscious but equally memorable meal at Mercado de Medellín food stalls in Roma (~$8–15 USD) for an authentic local send-off.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. Chapultepec is easily reachable by metro (Line 1, Chapultepec station). If departing the next day, pack bags the night before and confirm any airport transfers. Polanco is a 10-minute walk or short Uber from Chapultepec park.

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Benito Juárez International Airport to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation walk through the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), the heart of Mexico City. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace façade from the outside. Stop into the Palacio Nacional to view Diego Rivera's iconic murals depicting Mexican history — a free and breathtaking cultural experience just steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the illuminated streets of Centro Histórico as dusk falls — the colonial architecture is stunning at night. Head to the rooftop bar of Hotel Downtown or Terraza Catedral for artisanal cocktails and panoramic views of the Zócalo before dinner.

meals.lunch: Light welcome meal at Azul Histórico, a refined Mexican restaurant set in a beautiful courtyard garden in Centro Histórico. Try the chiles en nogada or the slow-braised lamb barbacoa tacos.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros, a celebrated contemporary Mexican restaurant in Centro Histórico known for pre-Hispanic ingredients and creative tasting menus. Reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing for a true luxury introduction to Mexican cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in confirmation with your hotel in advance. Carry some pesos for tips and small purchases. Centro Histórico is very walkable — most Day 1 activities are within a 10-minute walk of your hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Templo Mayor, the ancient Aztec ceremonial center excavated beneath Centro Histórico. Combine this with a visit to the adjacent Museo del Templo Mayor, which houses extraordinary artifacts including the famous Coyolxauhqui stone disc. A knowledgeable private guide will bring the layers of pre-Columbian history to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private car to Coyoacán neighborhood (20–25 min from Centro). Explore the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book a premium timed-entry ticket in advance to avoid crowds. Afterward, wander the charming cobblestone streets of Coyoacán, browse artisan markets, and visit the nearby Museo León Trotsky for a fascinating historical detour.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico or head to the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood for the evening. Explore Avenida Álvaro Obregón on foot, lined with Art Nouveau buildings, boutiques, and vibrant café culture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Café de Tacuba, one of Mexico City's oldest and most iconic cafés, just around the corner from the Zócalo. Try the chilaquiles verdes or enchiladas with hot chocolate.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Coyoacán at El Jardín del Pulpo or Los Danzantes Coyoacán — a sophisticated restaurant with an excellent mezcal selection and upscale Mexican dishes in a beautiful garden setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Contramar in Colonia Roma, arguably Mexico City's most beloved seafood restaurant. The tuna tostadas and grilled fish with two sauces are legendary. Reservations are essential — book weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets well in advance online — they sell out quickly. Consider hiring a bilingual private guide for Templo Mayor for a richer experience (~$80–120 USD). Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets in Coyoacán.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Teotihuacán (approx. 50 km northeast, ~1 hour by private car). Arrive early to beat the crowds and the midday heat. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and explore the Temple of the Feathered Serpent. Opt for a VIP hot air balloon ride over the pyramids at sunrise for a truly unforgettable luxury experience (must be pre-booked).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop at the upscale Polanco neighborhood — Mexico City's most glamorous district. Browse luxury boutiques along Presidente Masaryk Avenue (known as the 'Champs-Élysées of Mexico') and explore the stunning Museo Soumaya, a free, architecturally iconic museum housing one of the world's largest private art collections including works by Rodin, Dalí, and Monet.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Polanco, one of the city's premier dining and nightlife destinations. Walk through Parque Lincoln and enjoy the sophisticated atmosphere of this elegant neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel before departure to Teotihuacán — pack snacks or enjoy the on-site café at the archaeological zone.
meals.lunch: Lunch at La Gruta, a unique restaurant set inside a natural cave cavern at the Teotihuacán site — a memorable and atmospheric dining experience with traditional Mexican cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pujol, consistently ranked among the world's top 10 restaurants. Chef Enrique Olvera's tasting menu is a transcendent journey through modern Mexican cuisine — the mole madre, aged over 1,000 days, is iconic. This is the crown jewel of Mexico City dining. Reservations must be made months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The hot air balloon over Teotihuacán (offered by companies like Globos Aeroestáticos) typically departs at dawn — coordinate your private transfer accordingly. Wear sunscreen and a hat at Teotihuacán. Pujol reservations are extremely competitive; book the moment your trip is confirmed.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world. Marvel at the Aztec Sun Stone, the Maya room, and artifacts spanning Mexico's extraordinary pre-Columbian civilizations. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours. A private guide will make the experience deeply enriching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Bosque de Chapultepec, Mexico City's vast urban park, with a leisurely walk or private golf cart tour. Visit Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle), perched on a hilltop with sweeping city views and fascinating exhibits on Mexican imperial and presidential history. Afterward, take a private car to the San Ángel neighborhood to browse the famous Bazar del Sábado (if visiting on Saturday) or the permanent galleries and boutiques along its flower-lined streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Colonia Condesa, the city's bohemian-chic neighborhood, for an evening of stylish bars and world-class dining. Walk tree-lined Avenida Amsterdam, a unique oval boulevard, and soak in the neighborhood's European-influenced architecture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel's restaurant or at Expendio de Maíz Sin Nombre in Centro — a celebrated spot for traditional corn-based dishes and a true immersion into authentic Mexico City breakfast culture.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quintonil in Polanco, Chef Jorge Vallejo's acclaimed restaurant celebrating indigenous Mexican ingredients and seasonal cuisine. The tasting menu is extraordinary and slightly more accessible in feel than Pujol while equally world-class.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rosetta in Colonia Roma, a romantic Italian-Mexican fusion restaurant in a restored 19th-century mansion. Chef Elena Reygadas (named Latin America's Best Female Chef) creates exquisite pasta and seasonal dishes. The ambiance is intimate and luxurious.

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is best experienced with a private guide — budget 3 hours minimum. Chapultepec Castle has a separate entrance fee from the park. If Day 4 falls on a Saturday, the Bazar del Sábado in San Ángel is a must-visit for fine Mexican crafts and art.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat tour of the Xochimilco canals — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of Mexico City's most unique experiences. Board a colorfully decorated trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) for a private guided tour of the ancient Aztec chinampas (floating gardens). Arrange for a mariachi band to serenade you on the water and have local food vendors bring freshly made tlayudas, elotes, and tamales directly to your boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico for a curated luxury shopping experience. Visit Fonart (the national artisan fund store) for high-quality Mexican crafts, or explore the boutiques along Madero Street and the galleries around Palacio de Bellas Artes. Step inside the stunning Palacio de Bellas Artes for a final cultural visit — admire its Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and the murals by Rivera, Orozco, and Siqueiros inside.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Mexico City. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the rooftop bar of the Gran Hotel Ciudad de México, overlooking the Zócalo with its stunning stained-glass Tiffany ceiling visible from the lobby. End your trip with a final unforgettable dinner celebrating the flavors of Mexico.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at your hotel before heading to Xochimilco. Alternatively, visit Café El Popular in Centro Histórico, open 24 hours and beloved for its traditional Mexican breakfast spread.
meals.lunch: Enjoy a floating brunch on the trajinera in Xochimilco — arrange in advance with your tour operator to have a private chef or curated food vendors serve freshly prepared Mexican street food classics on the boat.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Sud 777 in Pedregal, Chef Edgar Núñez's innovative restaurant surrounded by volcanic rock gardens, offering a sophisticated modern Mexican tasting menu with outstanding wine and mezcal pairings. A perfect, memorable final night.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Xochimilco private boat experience through a reputable luxury tour operator to ensure a private trajinera, guide, and curated food/music arrangements — avoid the crowded public embarcaderos. Allow extra time for traffic returning from Xochimilco on weekend afternoons. Pack a light layer for evenings as March nights can be cool at Mexico City's altitude (2,240m / 7,350ft).
